rationale: Best-supported non-AI for the identified optional Workload Service Assurance feature: official HCL docs describe critical-job deadline calculation, promotion and resource prioritization, conventional scheduler behavior. HWA 10 also has AI anomaly-detection/Data Advisory capabilities, but retained evidence does not attribute them to this named feature; suite-wide features cannot be transferred without inclusion evidence. Broader product coverage and record version remain unknown; weak/forced rather than absence-based certainty.
version_scope: No source release/date; HCL feature docs are Workload Automation 10.2.6. 'Milestone #8' is not treated as a release identifier.
issues: Broader HWA AI capability applicability to this named optional feature is unresolved; no exhaustive included-feature coverage.

sources.excerpt: The workload service assurance feature is enabled and disabled by the global option enWorkloadServiceAssurance. It is enabled by default. ... calculates a critical start time ... promoted job is assigned additional operating system resources and its submission is prioritized.
sources.applicability: Official feature-specific HWA v10.2.6 documentation describes conventional scheduling operation, not the whole suite.

sources.excerpt: HWA 10 introduces AI-powered anomaly detection for workloads ... AI Data Advisory ... big data machine learning analytics technologies applied to the data from Workload Automation.
sources.applicability: Official broader HWA 10 AI context; retained source does not connect AI to named Service Assurance feature.

sources.excerpt: Workload service assurance is an optional feature that allows you to identify critical jobs and to ensure that they are processed in a timely manner. (Milestone #8)
sources.applicability: Exact named optional feature and assigned description; no product version supplied.
